subsystems.name: Textile body interface
subsystems.role: anchors the assistive force on the body and spreads it so it does not cut in or rub.
parts: woven or knitted cuffs and waist belt

subsystems.name: Actuation
subsystems.role: generates the pull that supplements the wearer's muscles.

subsystems.name: Transmission and anchors
subsystems.role: routes force from the actuator to the correct joint segment.
parts: attachment points at thigh, shank or back

subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: works out where the wearer is in a movement so assistance lands at the right instant.
parts: inertial measurement units on trunk and limb

subsystems.name: Control electronics
subsystems.role: runs the gait-phase or lift-onset estimator and modulates cable force.
parts: wireless link for tuning and logging

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: keeps the device running for a full shift or therapy session.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the task
buildSteps.detail: Motion capture, muscle activity and joint-torque measurements of the target activity (walking, lifting, prolonged standing) define how much help is needed and at which phase of the cycle.

buildSteps.title: Set the assistance profile
buildSteps.detail: Engineers decide whether to assist hip extension, hip flexion or back extension, and draw the desired force-versus-time curve the controller must track.

buildSteps.title: Design the textile interface
buildSteps.detail: Patterns are cut and sewn, then iterated through fit trials on varied body shapes; pressure mapping checks that force is spread across large areas rather than concentrated at the cable exits.

buildSteps.title: Bench-test the drivetrain
buildSteps.detail: Motor, spool and cable are run against a dummy load to measure delivered force, cable stretch, friction losses and acoustic noise before anyone wears it.

buildSteps.title: Build the sensing and control loop
buildSteps.detail: Inertial data is used to classify gait phase or detect lift onset in real time; the controller then closes a force loop on the cable tension with a delay low enough to feel natural.

buildSteps.title: Tune on human subjects
buildSteps.detail: Wearers walk or lift on instrumented treadmills and force plates; metabolic cost, muscle activity and joint load are compared with and without assistance to find when the device genuinely helps rather than just resisting.

buildSteps.title: Field and clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Shift-length trials with workers and supervised sessions with rehabilitation patients expose durability, donning time, comfort and fatigue problems that lab tests miss.

buildSteps.title: Productionise
buildSteps.detail: Cut-and-sew textile lines, actuator sub-assembly, per-unit calibration and washability/durability testing turn prototypes into a manufacturable product.

prerequisites.tech: Small, efficient brushless motors and gearboxes
prerequisites.why: a wearable actuator must deliver useful torque while staying light enough not to load the wearer.
shift-length operation needs high energy per kilogram on the body.
gait-phase and posture detection depend on cheap, tiny IMUs.
algorithms work well for steady walking but are less reliable across uneven ground, stairs and varied individuals.

prerequisites.tech: Textiles that transmit load without pressure injury
prerequisites.why: fabric anchors slip and concentrate force; keeping them comfortable over hours is unsolved engineering.
lab studies show modest reductions in effort, but long-term injury-prevention evidence in workplaces is still thin.

pathway.milestone: back-assist and hip-assist soft exosuits piloted in logistics, assembly and rehabilitation
pathway.unlocks: real user feedback on comfort, donning time and duty cycle.

pathway.milestone: adaptive control tuned per wearer and per task, plus multi-joint assistance
pathway.unlocks: useful help across varied movements rather than one rehearsed gait.

pathway.milestone: controlled clinical trials and regulatory clearance for rehabilitation use
pathway.unlocks: reimbursed use in stroke and mobility therapy.

pathway.milestone: textile-based artificial muscles replacing motor-and-cable drives
pathway.unlocks: garment-like devices with no rigid actuator box, lower weight and silent operation.
